title: VetoClub.AI (LetsPlanIt)
description: Plans group outings right inside your iMessage group chat, no separate app needed. It picks up on dates and preferences as your friends text, then chimes in when the group needs a nudge.
achievement: Full agentic workflow with silent extraction + active orchestration

title: Terminal Agent
description: Fixes your terminal mistakes before you have to go Google them. The moment a command fails, it looks up what likely went wrong and hands you a fix on the spot.
achievement: Intelligent error resolution with LLM-powered debugging

title: Interview.AI
description: Runs realistic mock technical interviews on demand. Talk or type your answers, solve live coding problems, and get follow-up questions that adapt to what you just said.
achievement: Multi-modal adaptive interviewing with live code execution

title: Dribble.AI
description: Watches soccer match footage and automatically tags the passes, shots, and momentum shifts a coach would care about, turning raw video into a searchable breakdown of the game.

title: FinLens
description: Pulls the key data out of financial documents automatically, no matter the format they come in, so teams stop retyping numbers from PDFs by hand.

title: DocuSense.AI
description: Lets you ask plain-English questions about your own documents, leases, offer letters, contracts, and get straight answers, all processed locally so nothing sensitive leaves your machine.

title: AgroTalk
description: Gives farmers weather-, soil-, and season-aware advice through a simple chat interface, so field decisions are backed by current conditions instead of guesswork.

title: Semantic Clustering for Model Cards
description: Turns HuggingFace's sprawling catalog of model cards into an interactive map, making it easy to browse and discover similar models instead of scrolling through search results.

title: Drawing-to-Data (D2D)
description: Reads engineering drawings the way an inspector would, spotting the relevant regions and pulling out the text, to speed up compliance checks that used to be done by hand.

title: Kaggriculture Agent
description: Plays Kaggle's farming-simulation game autonomously, planting, watering, harvesting, and selling a crop each round, with a local viewer to replay and review any match.

title: TA Buddy
description: Helps stuck students by tracing the question back to the concept they're actually missing, not just answering what was asked. Shows teachers where students are really struggling.
achievement: End-to-end diagnostic tutor, from concept mapping to grounded Socratic tutoring

title: Enterprise Risk Appliance
description: Lets access-risk analysts ask plain-English questions about who can do what across an enterprise system, and get answers backed by exact evidence, not a black-box guess.
achievement: Grounded, fully auditable AI investigations — zero fabricated risk findings by design

title: Campus Resale
description: Turns dorm move-out chaos into a real buy-low-sell-high operation. Feed it a listing and it estimates resale value, tells you what to offer, and walks you through negotiating down to a price that actually pencils out.
achievement: Deterministic pricing/profit engine with an LLM reasoning layer on top — zero hallucinated numbers by design

title: Prompt Engineer
description: Turns a vague business problem into one implementation-ready MVP build prompt, so product teams stop guessing between RAG, agents, workflows, or a plain app before a single line of code gets written. An adaptive Q&A interface interviews the user in plain business language, branching its questions based on prior answers, while deterministic gates check for missing requirements, contradictions, and scope gaps before anything gets compiled into a spec. The output is a single structured prompt an engineer or coding agent can hand straight to a build, with the architecture choice already justified by the requirements rather than picked by default. By separating what the business actually needs from how it eventually gets built, it cuts the two failure modes that sink most AI MVPs: over-engineering a simple problem into an agent framework it never needed, or under-engineering a genuinely stateful workflow into a brittle prompt-and-response loop that falls apart under real usage.
